newsitem.title: ITALY: RALLYING-SAINZ GAMBLE PAYS OFF BUT MCRAE STILL LEADS.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ GAMBLE PAYS OFF BUT MCRAE STILL LEADS.

text.p: Former world champion Carlos Sainz of Spain launched a stunning attack on the second leg of Italy's San Remo Rally on Tuesday, placing pressure on leader Colin McRae.
Ford driver Sainz had dropped to eighth overnight after deliberately checking in at the final control on Monday a minute late to incur a 10-second penalty.

Sainz gambled he would have better road conditions by starting later on Tuesday and although there was some rain, it paid off with the Spaniard reducing the deficit from 44 to 21 seconds in four stages and jumping to second place.
"The risk is the weather, but we have to push a bit," said Sainz.
Scotland's McRae, the 1995 world champion, said: "It's not as bad as yesterday. The road is cleaning up for the later runners."

Fellow Subaru driver Piero Liatti of Italy has dropped to third, unable to match the pace of the leaders, while Frenchman Didier Auriol lost fourth place when his Mitsubishi suffered a transmission problem that led to a huge spin on stage eight.
Andrea Dallavilla of Italy, the star of the first leg on Monday, dropped out of contention when he overturned his Toyota twice in separate accidents and lost four minutes.
Swede Kenneth Eriksson nipped past Bruno Thiry when the Belgian driver's Ford suffered electrical problems.
The 1,950 kms rally will probably be decided on the mountain roads close to San Remo on Wednesday, especially if the weather gets worse.
New world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland has been out of the running since Monday when he crashed his Mitsubishi, injuring his co-driver.
